correctness.rationale: Sun–Xu’s explicitly resolved F_3 pencil in characteristic 5 has 12 blowups and Picard rank 14. The fiber F=2C_0+6Γ−Σe, the t=0 strict transforms A,B and ten E_{a,i}=e_{a,i}−e_{a,i+1} (1≤i≤5), and the t=∞ component C_0 generate the 13-dimensional vertical subgroup. Independent SymPy determinantal computation on its complete 14×13 integer matrix yields rank13, maximal minors [0,24,−12,12,−12,12,−12,12,−12,12,−12,12,−12,12], gcd12. Inspected bundled verify.py identifies a 12×12 determinant ±1, hence SNF 1^12,12. Restriction from regular S to smooth generic C has vertical kernel, Pic(C)=Z⊕Z/12; horizontal final exceptional meets F once, supplying rational section and degree split, so J(k(t))=Z/12. This is an integral full-lattice computation, not rank-only inference; valid only for specified characteristic-5 fibration.

originality.rationale: Sun–Xu’s section 5 supplies full fiber geometry but not this precise MW torsion group. Earlier Saito/Nguyen constructions of related pencils and general Shioda/Gong–Xu rank methods do not state the characteristic-5 integral SNF nor force order12 from rank zero. Resultary returned no corresponding exact torsion statement. Literature priority risk persists for the older pencil papers, some full text unavailable.
residual_risks: Old Saito/Sakakibara and Nguyen 1994–95 pencil papers not inspected in full; historical exact torsion priority remains possible.
Relies on published characteristic-5 resolution/contact orders and horizontality of sixth exceptional curves; arithmetic independently verified conditional on these inputs.

value.rationale: The full Mordell–Weil group is a central arithmetic invariant of the newly explicit four-singular-fiber genus-two surface. Determining its exact torsion order 12 via an unsaturated vertical lattice is information not supplied by general rank formulas and naturally useful in comparing reductions and fibration arithmetic.
